_note: Every number and fact in heat.json points at keys here. 'checked' says what was read and when. Raw pages were saved by tools/heat_fetch.py into the git-ignored .refs/heat/ and read with tools/heat_read.py. Values computed by the page (RT, kT, multiples, odds, the ion pair in water) show their formula on the page and cite the constants they use.

nist-k.cite: NIST CODATA recommended values: Boltzmann constant k.

nist-r.cite: NIST CODATA recommended values: molar gas constant R.
nist-r.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: R = 8.314 462 618... J/(mol K), exact (R is k times the Avogadro constant).

nist-na.cite: NIST CODATA recommended values: Avogadro constant.
nist-na.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: N_A = 6.022 140 76 x 10^23 per mol, exact.

nist-e.cite: NIST CODATA recommended values: elementary charge e.

nist-ep0.cite: NIST CODATA recommended values: vacuum electric permittivity.

os-chem-7-5.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 7.5 Strengths of Ionic and Covalent Bonds.
os-chem-7-5.checked: 2026-10-01, Table 7.2 read: C-C 345, H-O 464, C-H 415, C=C 611 kJ/mol; bond energy is the energy needed to break a bond in one mole of gas molecules; 769 kJ separates one mole of solid NaCl into gaseous ions.

os-chem-10-1.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: hydrogen bonds are much weaker than covalent bonds, only about 5 to 10% as strong; hydrogen bonds are intermolecular, not covalent; van der Waals forces are all attractive forces between neutral atoms and molecules; dispersion forces are very weak but add up (geckos); A-T share two hydrogen bonds and C-G three; DNA strands unzip relatively easily because hydrogen bonds are weak compared with covalent bonds; boiling liquid HCl takes about 17 kJ/mol, breaking its covalent bonds about 430.

os-chem-9-5.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 9.5 The Kinetic-Molecular Theory.
os-chem-9-5.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: the average kinetic energy of a mole of gas molecules is KE_avg = (3/2)RT, directly proportional to kelvin temperature; raising the temperature raises the average speed and kinetic energy.

os-chem-12-5.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: Arrhenius equation k = A e^(-Ea/RT); the term e^(-Ea/RT) describes the effect of the energy barrier; a higher temperature gives a greater fraction of molecules with enough energy to cross it.

os-chem-10-3.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: enthalpy of fusion of ice 6.01 kJ/mol at 0 C; enthalpy of vaporization of water 40.67 kJ/mol at its boiling point, 44.01 kJ/mol at 25 C, 43.46 kJ/mol at 37 C (normal body temperature); while water boils its temperature stays constant.

os-up2-8-5.cite: OpenStax University Physics Volume 2, section 8.5 Molecular Model of a Dielectric (Table 8.1).
os-up2-8-5.checked: 2026-10-01, Table 8.1 read: dielectric constant of water 80, of vacuum 1.

os-bio-2-1.cite: OpenStax Biology 2e, section 2.1 Atoms, Isotopes, Ions, and Molecules: The Building Blocks.
os-bio-2-1.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: hydrogen bonds and van der Waals interactions are two weak bonds that occur often; single hydrogen bonds are weak and easily broken but occur in very large numbers; they zip the DNA double helix together; ionic bonds are not as strong as covalent; these bonds together give proteins their 3D shape.

os-bio-2-2.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: in liquid water hydrogen bonds constantly form and break; at the boiling point of 100 C the heat breaks the hydrogen bonds and molecules escape as gas; in ice a crystal held by hydrogen bonds forms, less dense than liquid; hydrogen bonding gives water its high heat capacity.

os-bio-3-4.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: changes in temperature, pH or chemicals can change a protein's shape without changing its primary sequence (denaturation); denaturation is often reversible but frying an egg is irreversible, the albumin in egg white denatures in a hot pan; not all proteins denature at high temperatures; alpha helices and beta sheets are held by hydrogen bonds.

os-bio-6-5.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: warmer generally speeds reactions, but temperatures outside an enzyme's optimal range affect bonds in the active site, and high temperatures eventually denature enzymes.

os-micro-10-2.cite: OpenStax Microbiology, section 10.2 Structure and Function of DNA.
os-micro-10-2.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: heat or chemicals can denature the double helix into single strands; cooling lets the hydrogen bonds re-form (renaturing); because of the extra hydrogen bond in each C-G pair, DNA with high GC content is harder to denature.

os-micro-12-2.cite: OpenStax Microbiology, section 12.2 Visualizing and Characterizing DNA, RNA, and Protein.
os-micro-12-2.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: in PCR, double-stranded DNA is denatured at approximately 95 C, then cooled to about 50 C, then held at 72 C for the heat-stable polymerase.

hz1v-1982.cite: Huang, Y. S., Hedberg, M., Kawanishi, C. Y. (1982). Characterization of the DNA of a nonoccluded baculovirus, Hz-1V. Journal of Virology 43, 174-181.
hz1v-1982.checked: 2026-10-01, abstract read (Europe PMC, PMID 16789226): thermal denaturation showed a high G+C part (about 11% of the genome) melting at Tm 97 C and the rest (89%) at 86.5 C, corresponding to G+C contents of 67% and 42%. The page uses these two measured points for its illustrative melting map.

gels-2025.cite: Wang, L., Li, R., Lv, S. et al. (2025). The Thermodynamic and Gelation Properties of Ovalbumin and Lysozyme. Gels 11, 470.
gels-2025.checked: 2026-10-01, abstract read (Europe PMC, PMID 40558770): ovalbumin and lysozyme are the main globular proteins of egg white; measured by differential scanning calorimetry in water (5% w/v, heated 5 C per minute) their denaturation temperatures were 80.22 C and 77.46 C; lysozyme refolded almost 100% on a second heating in water, while ovalbumin was completely denatured.

anderson-1990.cite: Anderson, D. E., Becktel, W. J., Dahlquist, F. W. (1990). pH-induced denaturation of proteins: a single salt bridge contributes 3-5 kcal/mol to the free energy of folding of T4 lysozyme. Biochemistry 29, 2403-2408.
anderson-1990.checked: 2026-10-01, abstract read (Europe PMC, PMID 2337607): one salt bridge between Asp70 and His31 stabilises the folded protein by 3 to 5 kcal/mol (12.6 to 20.9 kJ/mol at 4.184 kJ per kcal).

wiki-hbond.cite: Wikipedia, Hydrogen bond (section on strength, citing the IUPAC 2011 definition and textbook values).
wiki-hbond.checked: 2026-10-01, page source read: typical hydrogen bond energies O-H...N 29 kJ/mol (water to ammonia), O-H...O 21 kJ/mol (water to water), N-H...N 13 kJ/mol, N-H...O 8 kJ/mol (water to amide); strength varies with geometry and surroundings. Used because the OpenStax pages give only the relative strength (5 to 10% of a covalent bond).

wiki-vdw.cite: Wikipedia, Van der Waals force (section on strength, citing force field papers in J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2021 and Langmuir 2013).
wiki-vdw.checked: 2026-10-01, page source read: pairwise van der Waals attraction between H atoms of different H2 molecules 0.06 kJ/mol, between O atoms of different O2 molecules 0.44 kJ/mol, for more polarizable S atoms more than 1 kJ/mol.

wiki-saltbridge.checked: 2026-10-01, page source read: in water at moderate ionic strength, a 1:1 ion pair associates with a free energy of about 5 to 6 kJ/mol, about 8 kJ/mol at zero ionic strength, almost independent of the kind of ion; the N to O distance in a salt bridge is less than 4 angstroms (0.4 nm).

os-ap-24-6.cite: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 24.6 Energy and Heat Balance.
os-ap-24-6.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: the core temperature of the body stays steady at around 36.5 to 37.5 C (97.7 to 99.5 F).

medline-fever.cite: MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia (U.S. National Library of Medicine), Fever.
medline-fever.checked: 2026-10-01, page read: an adult probably has a fever when the temperature in the mouth is above 37.2 to 37.5 C, depending on the time of day; a cold can cause a high fever of 38.9 to 40 C; brain damage from a fever generally will not occur unless the fever is over 42 C.
